div.div: "1% FPR" is about 26 000 false alarms per home per month - a budget of 4 needs a per-window FPR near 1.5 x 10⁻⁶: fix the budget first
Per-window false-positive rate (log scale) and what it means at one decision per 1 s [1]

left: per-window FPR | right of axis: false
alarms per 30 days [2] (my arithmetic)

Research operating point: TPR at 1% FPR [B3]
= about 26 000 false windows per month (my arithmetic)

Product budget: an illustrative 4 false alarms per home per month [3]
-> per-window FPR near 1.5 x 10⁻⁶ if every false window counts

gap: about 3.8 orders of magnitude
(3 to 4, my arithmetic)
Partly closed by: merging touching false windows into one EVENT; requiring several positive windows in a row - both cost latency [C1]
The KPI ladder: four stages, same six KPIs at each [C1]

1 motion anywhere in the home?
hard part: non-human change

2 which room has motion?
hard part: adjacent rooms through walls

3 anyone home, moving or still?
hard part: a still person barely changes the CSI

4 which room is a person in?
hard part: both of the above

Six KPIs per stage: TPR, FPR, TNR, FNR (wrong room counts as a miss), BLIND-SPOT ratio (area or rooms where errors exceed a threshold), EFFECTIVE-COVERAGE ratio (area or rooms where TPR and TNR both pass). The last two turn an average into a map: a good average can still fail one room every day.

Time to detect (start of motion -> first positive) and time to clear (exit -> "empty"): report both as distributions with a high percentile, not a mean. State window-level vs event-level for every number.

Why it matters (ILLUSTRATIVE): a lab demo looked near-perfect before false-positive cases were tested; the later field study at the product budget reached about 0.5 TPR against a target of 0.9 [4]. Causes: CSI outliers, drift over time, chip CSI quality [C1].

Legend: red = research operating point / field shortfall | green = product budget, stage 1 | blue, amber, red stages = increasing difficulty | grey ticks = false alarms per 30 days at that FPR. Report every KPI per scenario (near a device, near the AP, door, far, room with no device, small motion, still, empty) [C1, C2].

Numbers (all loaded from constants.json):
[1] window_short_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; round analysis window used in early single-link work; internal I1/I2
[2] seconds_per_30_days - public; arithmetic: 30 x 86400
[3] false_alarm_budget_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; illustrative product-level false-alarm budget; internal I7
[4] field_tpr_vs_target_illustrative - ILLUSTRATIVE; illustrative field shortfall at a false-alarm budget of a few per month; internal I7
Arithmetic (my arithmetic, as in [C1]): decisions per 30 days = seconds_per_30_days / window; false windows at 1% FPR = 0.01 x that; budget FPR = budget / decisions. Notes: [B3] TPR at fixed FPR; [C1] KPIs; [C2] scenario taxonomy. Public ref: Fawcett 2006 (ROC).
